tagline: Taiwan's harbour city already commutes by water — millions cross to Cijin every year. Now make it fast, clean and foiling.
summary: Kaohsiung is Taiwan's great southern port-city, and it is one of the rare places that already moves people across its harbour by boat: the Cijin Island ferries carry a heavy daily commuter and visitor flow, and the city is reinventing its waterfront through the Asia New Bay Area redevelopment. The water-commuting habit is already adopted — the opportunity is to modernise it with fast, smooth, all-electric foiling — and to reach out along the Kenting resort coast and across to the Penghu islands.

use_cases.title: Modernise the Cijin commute
use_cases.body: Replace the diesel harbour ferries on the Gushan/Sizihwan↔Cijin crossings with fast, near-silent all-electric foiling shuttles — upgrading an already-adopted daily water commute rather than creating demand from scratch.

use_cases.title: Asia New Bay waterfront circuit
use_cases.body: A foiling loop linking the cruise terminal, Pier-2 arts district, Love River mouth and Cijin turns the redeveloping harbour into a connected leisure-transit surface for visitors and residents.

use_cases.title: Kenting resort-coast & Liuqiu hops
use_cases.body: Foiling transfers down the coast to the Kenting resort arc and out to Xiaoliuqiu (via Donggang) give premium travellers a smooth alternative to the long road trip south.

use_cases.title: Kaohsiung ↔ Penghu fast island link
use_cases.body: A hybrid Quanta-LR service crosses the ~75 nm to Magong, replacing a 4.5-hour conventional ferry with a fast, smooth island connection — and removing weather-fragility on the open Taiwan Strait.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Owns the harbour and near-coast network: the Cijin commuter crossings, the Asia New Bay waterfront circuit, and coastal hops toward Kenting and Xiaoliuqiu — all short, dense and well within the 70 nm all-electric range.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Carries the open-water island line to Penghu (Kaohsiung↔Magong, ~75 nm) — beyond the all-electric envelope and across the exposed Taiwan Strait, where hybrid range and refuel-anywhere operation give the reliability margin a conventional ferry lacks.

competitive_landscape: Kaohsiung is one of the few Asian cities where harbour commuting by boat is already routine — the Cijin ferries carry millions a year — alongside a Love River tourist boat and scheduled crossings to Xiaoliuqiu and Penghu. These diesel services are the proof of demand and the status quo to improve on: the commute exists, the volume is real, and none of it is fast, clean or foiling yet.
seasonality: Southern Taiwan runs two seasonal stresses: the summer typhoon season (roughly Jun–Oct) and the winter NE monsoon, which makes the open Taiwan Strait crossing to Penghu rough and cancellation-prone. The sheltered harbour commute is workable year-round; foiling adds smoothness in chop, and the Quanta-LR hybrid is the answer to the strait's weather-fragility.
regulatory_note: Harbour operations sit under the Taiwan International Ports Corporation (TIPC) and the Kaohsiung City Marine Bureau, with the MOTC Maritime and Port Bureau on national rules — a single municipal/port authority can anchor a clean-fleet pilot tied to the Asia New Bay Area redevelopment. Route planning respects the naval facilities at Zuoying; keep all framing to domestic Taiwan waters and recognised island links.

precedents.why_it_matters: Shows a phased clean-foiling network is deliverable across islands and a busy harbour — directly relevant to upgrading Kaohsiung's existing ferry volume.

internal.sovereign_channel: TIPC is the sovereign counterparty that gates the bay; Kaohsiung City Marine Bureau runs the ferries. Asia New Bay Area 2025–28 is the pedestal design-in window. Horizon Yachts / Ocean Alexander = local composite-MRO adjacency.
internal.cross_border_notes: Keep ALL framing to domestic Taiwan waters and recognised island links (Penghu, Xiaoliuqiu, Kenting). Do NOT author any cross-strait mainland-China route on this public brief — asymmetric-recognition zone.

deck_only.narrative: Kaohsiung is the strongest 'modernise an adopted habit' transit anchor in the East Asia set — the harbour already commutes by boat — bundled with a waterfront redevelopment, a resort coast, and an island line-haul.
